modules.title: Welcome to Station
modules.outcome: Say who you are and how Station works, in one breath.

lessons.title: Who you are on a call
lessons.goal: Introduce yourself honestly as an independent partner.
lessons.read_md:
**Sample lesson.** The real course replaces this text.

You're an **independent partner with Station**. Station builds, sets up and supports everything; you're the business owner's contact.

- Say your name.
- Say you're an independent partner with Station.
- Give the reason in a few words, then ask if it's a good time.

> "Hi, it's Sam, an independent partner with Station, calling about missed calls. Did I catch you at a bad time?"

check.q: A roofer asks, "So you're with Station?" You say:
options: "I'm an independent partner with Station. Station builds and supports everything, and I'm your contact."
check.why: You're independent, not an employee, and you never handle accounts.

check.q: What do you do in the first 15 seconds?
options: Name, independent partner, the reason, and ask if it's a good time.
Read out every product so they know the options.
check.why: Who you are, why you're calling, and permission. Nothing else yet.

lessons.title: Support is Station's
lessons.goal: Pass every support question to Station the same day.
lessons.read_md:
**Sample lesson.** Support is always Station's. When a client asks you to fix something, tell them Station will handle it and pass it on with **Message Station** the same business day.

You never log into a client's account, and you never take a password.

check.q: A client texts: "Can you just log in and fix my hours?" You:
options: Tell her Station will handle it and pass it on with Message Station today.
Note it for the end of the week.
check.why: Support goes to Station the same business day. You never log in for a client.

modules.title: The money
modules.outcome: Explain exactly when and how you're paid.

lessons.title: When you earn
lessons.goal: Know that a free trial earns nothing.
lessons.read_md:
**Sample lesson.** You earn when a client's payment **clears**. A free trial earns nothing; commission starts with the first real payment.

| What happens | What you earn |
|---|---|
| Free trial | Nothing |
| First payment clears | Your share of it |
| Hosting & care | Nothing |

check.q: A salon starts a free trial through your link today. What do you earn in the trial?
options: Nothing. Commission starts when the first real payment clears.
Your full share, on the day they sign up.
check.why: Nothing is earned during a free trial.

lessons.title: No promises
lessons.read_md:
**Sample lesson.** Never promise a result: no jobs, calls, reviews, rankings or money. Say what it does, not what it will earn them.

> "I can't promise a number, because it depends on your business. What I can show you is exactly what it does."

check.q: The owner asks, "How many more jobs will I get?" You say:
options: "I can't promise a number. I can show you exactly what it does."
"It pays for itself in a week."
check.why: No promises, ever: say what it does.

modules.title: Who buys
modules.outcome: Spot the one problem a business has and name the smallest fix.

lessons.title: Start with the gap
lessons.goal: Ask about the problem before you name a product.
lessons.read_md:
**Sample lesson.** Open with a question about the gap, not the product.

1. Ask what happens when the phone rings and nobody can answer.
2. Let the owner talk.
3. Then name **one** product that fixes what they told you.

check.q: Your first question to a plumber should be about:
options: What happens to a caller when he's under a house.
check.why: Start with what the gap costs them, not the product.

lessons.title: When you don't know
lessons.goal: Say Station can confirm it, and don't guess.
lessons.read_md: **Sample lesson.** When an owner asks something you don't know (an integration, a law, a feature), say: "Station can confirm that. I don't want to guess." Then pass it on.

check.q: "Does it work with Housecall Pro?" You don't know. You say:
options: "Station can confirm how it fits. I don't want to guess."
check.why: Never invent a feature or an integration.

quiz.q: A client asks you to log in and change her hours. You:
options: Pass it to Station with Message Station the same day.
Tell her to read the help pages.

quiz.q: What does a free trial earn you?

options: "I can't promise a number; here's what it does."
What happens when the phone rings and nobody answers.

quiz.q: You don't know if it works with their software. You say:
options: "Station can confirm that. I don't want to guess."

mock_call.brief_md: **Sample.** A recorded role-play of one full first call: you pitching a business. Ask a friend or family member to play the owner and give them the owner's sheet. **6 minutes at most**, one take, no edits.
must: Say your name and that you're an **independent partner with Station**, give the reason, and ask if it's a good time.
Ask two or three questions about the gap and let the owner talk.
Offer **one** product that fixes what they named, at its published price, said once.
Say you **earn a commission**, before you ask for anything.
Close: send the page, get an email, and name the **day and time** you'll check back.

scenarios.title: Dave's Heating & Plumbing
scenarios.you_see_md: HVAC and plumbing, four techs. **Why them:** calls go to voicemail during the day.
scenarios.owner_sheet_md: You're 47 and under a house most of the day. Raise one worry: "Will it sound like a robot?" Your wife does the books; if asked who decides, say "Me, but I'd show her."

rubric.label: Says who they are, honestly
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "Hi, it's Sam, an independent partner with Station, calling about missed calls. Did I catch you at a bad time?"

rubric.label: Discloses the commission
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "I'm paid a commission if you go ahead, so I'll be straight with you."

rubric.label: Starts with the gap, lets the owner talk
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "When you're under a house and the phone rings, what happens to that caller?"

rubric.label: One problem, the smallest fix, said like a name
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "Sounds like the missed calls are the real problem, so let's start there."

rubric.label: Published price, said once, no deals
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: The live price from station.solutions, said once.

rubric.label: No promises
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "I can't promise a number, because it depends on your business."

rubric.label: Handles the worry truthfully
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "Station can confirm that, I don't want to guess."

rubric.label: Finds who decides
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "Who else weighs in on something like this? I can send the page to them too."

rubric.label: Page, email, a dated next step
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "I'll check back Thursday at 10. Does that work?"

rubric.label: Stays out of the setup and the data
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "Station emails you the checkout link, then you book a short onboarding call."
